questions.q: What does a quant researcher primarily spend their time doing?
options: Designing and backtesting trading signals and models, relying heavily on statistics and machine learning
Executing trades and managing intraday risk in live markets
Building and maintaining execution infrastructure
Negotiating client contracts for a bank's trading desk
questions.explain: A quant researcher forms hypotheses about market patterns, builds models to capture them, and rigorously backtests them — a role leaning heaviest on statistics, probability, and machine learning.

questions.q: Which role is described as leaning heaviest on software engineering?
options: Quant trader
Quant researcher
Quant developer
Chief Risk Officer
questions.explain: A quant developer builds and maintains the infrastructure research and trading run on — data pipelines, backtesting frameworks, execution systems — requiring strong software engineering skills.

questions.q: What does 'overfitting' mean in the context of backtesting a trading model?
options: Running a backtest for too short a historical period
Building a model that fits past data too closely to generalize well to future, unseen data
Using too much computing power to run a backtest
Trading a strategy with too much leverage
questions.explain: Overfitting happens when a model captures noise or coincidental patterns in historical data rather than a genuine, repeatable relationship, so it performs well in the backtest but poorly going forward.

questions.q: What does a quant trader primarily need beyond technical fluency?
options: A law degree
Market intuition and decisiveness to manage intraday risk under live conditions
Expertise in tax accounting
A background exclusively in corporate law
questions.explain: A quant trader executes strategies and manages risk in real time, which requires market intuition and quick decision-making on top of enough technical understanding of the models being traded.

questions.q: How does firm size typically affect how distinct the researcher, developer, and trader roles are?
options: Firm size has no effect on role structure
Larger firms tend to have one person doing all three roles
Smaller firms often have one person covering two or more of the three roles, while larger firms tend to keep them as separate job titles
Only hedge funds ever separate these roles; banks never do
questions.explain: At large banks or established hedge funds these are often distinct titles with separate reporting lines, while at smaller shops one person frequently covers two or all three roles.
